tabs.title: Understanding the message
tabs.description: Interpret the writer's purpose and feelings.

tabs.title: Responding appropriately
tabs.description: Choose a response supported by the message.

questions.q: What does Ben's description of Greenhill tell Maya?
choices: It is a noisy city with no parks.
He has a friendly new home but still misses her.
He has returned to their old school.
He dislikes every part of his new town.
questions.explanation: Ben says Greenhill is quiet and friendly, but he misses lunches and games with Maya.

questions.q: Why does Ben write about the film night?
choices: He wants Maya to buy tickets for his sister.
He wants Maya to bring her own camera.
He wants to cancel their next meeting.
He hopes Maya can visit and spend the evening with him.
questions.explanation: Ben explains the free film night and how Maya could join him.

questions.q: Why do people sit on the grass with blankets?
choices: They are waiting for a football match.
The café has no chairs for visitors.
The film is shown outside in the park.
They have come to clean the park.
questions.explanation: The park film night takes place outdoors, so people bring blankets.

questions.q: What does Ben show by offering a blanket and mentioning warm clothes?
choices: He wants Maya to feel comfortable if she visits.
He expects Maya to bring food for everyone.
He does not want Maya to take the train.
He plans to move the film to his home.
questions.explanation: Ben offers help and warns that the evening will be cold.

questions.q: Why does Ben say his father can meet Maya at the station?
choices: His father works at the station.
Maya may need help getting from the train to the park.
He wants Maya to stay at the station all evening.
The film will be shown on the train.
questions.explanation: Ben offers an easy plan for Maya's arrival, including a meeting at five.

questions.q: What does the hot chocolate and popcorn stand help?
choices: Ben's school football team.
The train station.
The park, through the money from sales.
The actors in the film.
questions.explanation: The message says the money from the stand helps the park.

questions.q: What will change if the weather is bad?
choices: Maya will have to buy a more expensive ticket.
Ben will watch the film alone.
The film will start a week later.
The film will be shown at the youth centre.
questions.explanation: Ben gives a different indoor location if it rains.

questions.q: Maya wants to visit but is free only after Thursday. What should she do?
choices: Wait until Saturday evening to tell Ben.
Write before Thursday as Ben requests, or explain why she cannot.
Ask Eva to send Ben a reply for her.
Travel without telling Ben she is coming.
questions.explanation: Ben asks Maya to reply before Thursday so he can know her plans.

questions.q: Maya cannot go to Greenhill on Saturday. Which reply fits Ben's message?
choices: Thank Ben and tell him she is busy, then share news of her class.
Tell Ben he should not invite her to other events.
Ignore the invitation because she cannot attend.
Ask Ben to give his sister's ticket to another person.
questions.explanation: Ben says he understands if Maya is busy and wants news about her class as well.

questions.q: What is the most important thing Ben wants from Maya, besides a visit?
choices: A photograph of the park.
A new football for Eva.
A list of films she likes.
A reply that tells him how Maya is doing.
questions.explanation: The final lines ask Maya to write about her new class rather than just read his news.
